item.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
item.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. item.title: 2027: INEC REC seeks traditional rulers’ support for peaceful, secure elections in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, has called on traditional rulers in the state to promote a peaceful and secure environment before and during the 2027 general elections. Idris made the appeal during a courtesy visit to the Tor Tiv and Chairman of the Benue State Council of Traditional Rulers, His Royal Majesty, Orcivirigh Prof. James Ayatse, on Friday, November 20, 2026, as part of the Commission’s stakeholder engagement ahead of the elections. The REC also solicited the support of the traditional institution in encouraging eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and strengthening collaboration with INEC to ensure successful conduct of the forthcoming polls. According to a statement by the Public Affairs Officer of INEC in Benue State, Mrs. Peace Ogoyi, Idris described the visit as a vital step in the Commission’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “He solicited the intervention and support of the royal father in three key areas: encouraging the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), promoting a peaceful and secure environment before and during the elections, and providing further support to the Commission through sustained collaboration.” Responding, the Tor Tiv welcomed the REC and his delegation, expressing appreciation for the visit and acknowledging the important role of traditional rulers in ensuring a conducive environment for electoral activities. He noted that “traditional rulers, as fathers of the state, have a responsibility to receive electoral officials and ensure their safety and provision of a peaceful working environment. Drawing from his experience in previous elections, including his service in various ad hoc capacities and as a State Returning Officer, Ayatse acknowledged the enormous responsibilities confronting the Commission. He said the Traditional Council had consistently advocated peaceful political campaigns and a level playing field for all political parties. The monarch further disclosed that traditional and religious leaders had organised prayers for peaceful elections and maintained constructive engagements with security agencies to strengthen peace and security across the state. He assured the REC that the Council would continue to collaborate with relevant stakeholders to identify and address electoral security flashpoints ahead of the elections. On the credibility of the electoral process, the Tor Tiv emphasised the need for INEC to uphold the will of the people, urging the Commission’s personnel to discharge their duties with neutrality, fairness and professionalism. item.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
item.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished. Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical. In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra. In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports. Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations. item.title: Four die, 24 rescued as Bayelsa burial boat capsizes
item.description: Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday. Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie. The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized. Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment. The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation. He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders. Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for. item.title: UNICEF raises alarm over 624,000 out-of-school children
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised concerns over the high number of out-of-school children in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states, disclosing that about 624,000 children have been identified as being outside the classroom across the three states. The organisation said although about 68,000 children had benefited from interventions to return them to school, the scale of the challenge required urgent government action, increased investment and stronger community mobilisation. UNICEF’s Chief of Field Office in Sokoto, Dr Michael Juma, made this known at a media briefing organised by the organisation’s Sokoto Field Office as part of activities marking the 2026 World Children’s Day. He called for coordinated action by governments, media organisations, traditional institutions, religious leaders and community stakeholders to address challenges confronting children in the region. Juma urged journalists across the three states to intensify public enlightenment, investigative reporting and advocacy to promote children’s rights, strengthen government accountability and ensure access to education, healthcare, nutrition and other essential services. Describing the media as a critical partner in advancing children’s rights, he said journalists must go beyond reporting events to exposing gaps in service delivery and holding relevant authorities accountable. “The media are important duty-bearers in advancing children’s rights. Journalists must provide balanced coverage that highlights development achievements while drawing attention to persistent gaps affecting the wellbeing of children,” he said. He reaffirmed UNICEF’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with the governments of Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara, development partners, traditional and religious leaders, and grassroots organisations to guarantee children access to quality and inclusive education, healthcare, adequate nutrition, safe drinking water and social protection. Providing an account of interventions undertaken through UNICEF’s partnerships with the three state governments, Juma disclosed that approximately 98,000 children had benefited from the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) programme, designed to improve foundational literacy and numeracy. He said the organisation was also supporting teacher professional development, provision of instructional materials, accelerated basic education, integrated Qur’anic education and innovative learning opportunities, including radio-based education and the Nigeria Learning Passport. According to him, the interventions are particularly targeted at children affected by insecurity, displacement and other emergencies. On healthcare and immunisation, Juma disclosed that approximately 7.8 million children across the three states had been reached through measles-rubella vaccination, while more than five million children were vaccinated during the last concluded polio immunisation campaign. item.title: ‘Issakaba Returns’ grosses N47.8m in opening weekend, sets new record for Nollywood action thriller
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The highly anticipated Nollywood classic, “Issakaba Returns” stormed the domestic box office, recording a spectacular opening weekend gross of N47.8 million to become the highest-grossing debut ever for an action thriller. The film, directed by popular filmmaker and producer, Lancelot Oduwa Imasuen, premiered last Wednesday at Silverbird Cinemas, Victoria Island, Lagos. Celebrating the feat, Lancelot, fondly called D’Guvnor, thanked everyone who showed up, bought tickets, filled the cinemas and embraced “Issakaba Returns” with so much love. “To everyone who has supported this journey, shared the excitement, spread the word and made the opening weekend this remarkable, I do not take your love for granted. “This is more than numbers. It is a testament to the love, nostalgia and connection you all have with this story. “N47.8 million opening weekend gross, and this is only the beginning! “Thank you for believing in us. Thank you for showing up. The love has been organic, and we feel every bit of it,” Lancelot said. The premiere of “Issakaba Returns” was spectacular and memorable. The evening exploded into war songs, cultural dance and gyration as the film began its cinema run. Long before the lights went down inside the cinema hall, the carnival had already begun outside. Drummers, dancers and chanting fans set the mood, recreating the fearless spirit of the Issakaba Boys who, 25 years ago, stood against evil in the South-East. For the lead character, Sam Dede, the return is more than nostalgia. It is a message. Speaking at the premiere, he said the evils the Issakaba Boys fought a quarter of a century ago, kidnapping, money rituals, human trafficking are still ravaging society today. First released in 2001 and inspired by real-life vigilante movements, the original “Issakaba” became a cultural phenomenon. item.title: Davido and Chioma: The love story continues
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Afrobeats superstar Davido is known for flaunting his wife, Chioma Adeleke, on social media, displaying public affection and storming international show venues in her company. It is no surprise, therefore, that the three-time Grammy nominee has taken their romance to the studio, borrowing a leaf from the likes of Adekunle Gold and Simi, Banky W and Adesuwa Etomi, as well as Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who have all turned their love stories into music. For Davido, Chioma has never just been his wife. She has been his muse from the very beginning. Their love story in music started in 2018 with ‘Assurance’, the birthday gift Davido dedicated to Chioma when they were still dating. Chioma starred in the video, and the song became one of the most iconic love anthems in Afrobeats history. She returned in 2020 for ‘1 Milli’, whose wedding-themed video further celebrated their relationship. Nearly eight years after ‘Assurance’, ‘Already Falling’ brings that story full circle, from young lovers to husband and wife. The song, the eighth track on Davido’s sixth studio album, “ORIADÉ”, was released on July 31, 2026. It blends English, Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, and reimagines Elvis Presley’s timeless classic ‘Can’t Help Falling in Love’ through an Afrobeats lens with background vocals by Peruzz The official video, released on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, stars Chioma as his leading lady once again. Directed by Meji Alabi, who also directed ‘Assurance, the video was filmed at the historic Château de Chanteloup, the estate of French cognac house Maison Martell in Cognac, France. It blends French elegance with Nigerian style, with Davido arriving in a horse-drawn carriage, serenading Chioma in grand interiors, and later recreating a proposal scene by a lake at dusk, where he goes down on one knee to present her with a ring. Though the couple wedded in a lavish Lagos ceremony in June 2024, the proposal scene is a cinematic metaphor for renewed commitment, not a new engagement. Davido announced the release himself with the caption: “Already Falling. From us to you. Enjoy.” Like other music stars, Davido is proving that a real-life love story can become a powerful artistic brand. For fans, ‘Already Falling’ is more than a music video. It is a continuation of a story they have followed since 2018 ; from young lovers, to husband and wife, to parents, told in Davido’s most personal songs. And with Chioma by his side in the studio, on screen, and on tour, including their recent high-profile trip to Tanzania with Diamond Platnumz, the couple shows no signs of slowing down. item.title: Soludo approves N50,000 December bonus for Anambra workers
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has approved a N50,000 December bonus for civil servants in the state, with the payment expected to reflect in their December 2026 salaries. The governor announced the bonus during the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex in Awka, where he also approved measures to improve the working environment and productivity of civil servants. Soludo acknowledged the economic challenges facing workers, admitting that their current salaries were inadequate amid prevailing economic conditions. He, however, assured the workers that his administration would only make financial commitments it could realistically fulfil. “I understand the situation and economic conditions, that we need to be able to do something. The pay that we have all over is not enough; I clearly understand it. “But there is one thing I also want to tell you, and that is I don’t play to the wind. Before we get into a commitment, we make sure that it is something that we will always honour,” he said. Addressing comparisons between Anambra’s salary structure and those of other states, the governor urged civil servants to consider the different revenue bases and economic capacities of state governments before making such assessments. He stressed that sustainable governance and responsible financial management, rather than unfulfilled promises, remained the guiding principles of his administration. Soludo also expressed appreciation to the workers for their support during last year’s governorship election, saying he was pleased that public servants overwhelmingly voted for his administration in recognition of its developmental efforts. Responding to three major requests presented by the workers at the event, the governor immediately directed the rehabilitation of roads within the secretariat complex, approved the establishment of an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Centre and authorised the pruning of overgrown trees across the premises. Earlier, the Anambra State Head of Service, Barr. Ngozi Iwouno, commended Soludo for restoring security and normalcy across the state. She said civil servants could now attend work regularly without fear, noting that the disruption previously caused by Monday sit-at-home orders had been overcome. Iwouno said the improved security situation had restored confidence among workers and enabled them to discharge their duties more consistently. item.title: Passengers fear proposed biometric checks may cause chaos at domestic airports
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Federal Government’s proposed mandatory biometric checks for domestic air passengers from January 1, 2027, have come under scrutiny less than five days after the plan was announced, with passengers and industry observers warning that the policy could make air travel more difficult. They insisted that the plan appeared rushed and had not been properly thought through, particularly as the festive travel season would still be ongoing when the policy takes effect. They also feared that its implementation could trigger a repeat of the chaos that followed the introduction of the Go Cashless payment system, which caused hours of gridlock at airports in Lagos and Abuja. In March, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, introduced an electronic payment system known as Go Cashless at the toll gate of two of the country’s busiest airports. Its rollout left passengers travelling through the airports in Lagos and Abuja stranded for hours, triggering massive gridlock, missed flights and widespread frustration. While some travellers abandoned their vehicles at airport entrances after encountering difficulties completing payments, others said they missed scheduled flights after spending hours trying to gain access to the airports. The disruption prompted President Bola Tinubu to order the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, to announce a suspension of the system on the fourth day of its implementation. With the busy Yuletide travel period extending into January, passengers and industry observers fear that a similar situation could unfold at the Lagos airport, the country’s busiest, especially as Keyamo has given domestic airlines until December 31, 2026, to integrate their operations with the system that will facilitate the biometric checks. Keyamo warned that airlines that fail to comply with the directive would not be allowed to board passengers from January 1, 2027. Known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, v-PASS, the biometric identity verification system is linked to the National Identification Number, NIN, of Nigerians. It is designed exclusively for domestic flights, with all passengers required to provide their NIN during check-in. Passengers are also expected to pay additional charges for the service. Speaking during the unveiling of the system at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, Keyamo said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it. item.title: Pa Fasoranti for burial Dec 17; Ondo govt unveils 8-day programme
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, AKURE The Ondo State Government has released an eight-day programme of burial activities for the late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, CFR, with his funeral service and interment scheduled for Thursday, December 17, 2026. The programme, signed by the Chairman and Secretary of the State Burial Committee, Dr Kayode Ajulo and Apostle Eniola Olushola, Esq, respectively, shows that the ceremonies will begin on Sunday, December 13, with a cultural heritage day in honour of the deceased, who was born on May 11, 1926 and died on October 20, 2026. The opening ceremony, scheduled for 12 noon, will feature a showcase of Ondo State’s cultural heritage at the Dr Olusegun Mimiko International Centre for Culture and Events (The Dome), Akure. A commendation service will hold at Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, at 9.00 am on Monday, December 14, followed by a novelty football match in Fasoranti’s honour at the Akure Township Stadium. The football fixtures will see Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, take on St Frances, Akure, at 2.00 pm, while Akure High School will face Ondo Boys High School at 4.00 pm. Activities on Tuesday, December 15, will feature a symposium, national tribute and academic award at The Dome, Akure. The symposium, themed “A Selfless Cradle Light That The Yoruba Race Can’t Forget In A Hurry”, will be organised by Afenifere, the DAWN Commission and the Ondo State Government. It is scheduled for 10.00 am and will be followed by a national tribute and academic award. A lying-in-state and Christian wake-keep will take place at the deceased’s country home, Omolere Close, Akure, at 4.00 pm on Wednesday, December 16. The funeral service will hold at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Thursday, December 17, with interment to follow immediately at the church cemetery. A reception and entertainment of guests will subsequently hold at designated venues for the different categories of guests. The programme will continue on Friday, December 18, with a thanksgiving service at Akure Central Mosque at 1.00 pm, while Saturday, December 19, has been set aside for family visits to Baba’s residence. The final activity, an outing and thanksgiving service, will hold at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Sunday, December 20. item.title: ‘Leadership should not depend on luck’ – Okoroama on preparing technical experts for management
item.description: By Ayo Taiwo Nigerian engineering leader and business psychology specialist James Okoroama has introduced a leadership development model aimed at helping technically accomplished professionals navigate the challenges of transitioning into management. Okoroama presented his N-Curve Leadership Model at the 2026 Annual Conference of the Society for Maintenance & Reliability Professionals (SMRP), held in Raleigh, North Carolina, from September 28 to October 1. His presentation, titled “Leading Through the Dip: From Technical Expertise to Maintenance and Reliability Engineering Leadership Mastery,” examined why professionals who excel in technical roles sometimes struggle when promoted into leadership positions. The N-Curve model describes a transition in which employees may experience a temporary decline in confidence, effectiveness or perceived competence as they move from technical responsibilities to managing people and organisational performance. According to Okoroama, technical expertise does not automatically translate into the ability to lead teams, delegate responsibilities and develop other professionals. “We promote people for being the best fixer in the room, then ask them to stop fixing,” Okoroama said. “Of course there is a dip. The mistake is pretending it will not happen.” The model outlines a progression from technical mastery through promotion and a potential leadership dip, followed by adaptation and eventual leadership proficiency. Okoroama said that the transition requires professionals to move beyond individual technical achievements and develop skills in delegation, communication, coaching, conflict resolution and performance management. He introduced the model in a December 2025 research paper alongside a complementary framework known as the Situational Reliability Leadership Matrix, which proposes tailoring leadership development to individual readiness and organisational demands. His interest in the subject draws partly from his professional journey, which began with technical apprenticeship in Nigeria before progressing through equipment maintenance, reliability engineering, consulting and engineering management. He currently serves as a senior regional reliability engineering and robotics leader at Amazon, where he leads a technical organisation of more than 600 professionals supporting industrial automation and robotics operations. In 2026, he also serves as an RME Engagement and Workforce Development Strategy Partner within Amazon’s North America Customer Fulfillment network. Okoroama holds a Master of Science degree from the University of South Wales, where his studies explored the relationship between human behaviour, organisational performance and leadership. The research has implications for Nigerian organisations across manufacturing, energy, telecommunications and other sectors where technically skilled employees are frequently promoted into supervisory positions without sufficient leadership preparation. item.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Peru
item.description: A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities. The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers. Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.” Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.” AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake. The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao. Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.” Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.” Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them. A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes. item.title: Why obesity hits men harder than women – Study
item.description: By Shola Ogundipe Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological difference in the fat tissue of males and females that could help explain why obesity triggers different health consequences in men and women. The discovery suggests that the battle against obesity may be playing out differently beneath the skin, with immune cells living inside body fat either helping to protect against inflammation and metabolic disorders or making them worse, depending on biological sex. Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, US, found that a group of immune cells known as eosinophils, traditionally associated with allergies and asthma, perform different functions in the fat tissue of male and female mice. While certain populations of these cells appear to protect against obesity-related inflammation, others may contribute to harmful metabolic changes. The study, titled “Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity”, was funded by the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine. The findings, published in the journal PNAS Nexus, challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar in structure and function. They also raise questions about whether obesity treatments targeting the immune system should be designed differently for men and women. Led by biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik, the study used high-resolution single-cell sequencing to examine how individual immune cells behave in fat tissue. What emerged was an unexpected picture. The researchers identified six distinct populations of eosinophils in adipose tissue, each with its own genetic activity and potentially different biological functions. The discovery suggests that these cells are not simply passive occupants of body fat. Some may help maintain metabolic health, while others may contribute to the inflammatory processes associated with obesity. “Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought,” said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences at UCR’s School of Medicine. She explained that identifying and activating the biological pathways responsible for producing protective eosinophils could open new possibilities for improving metabolic health. But perhaps the most striking finding was the difference between male and female mice. Female mice had a population of eosinophils that appeared to work more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells found in fat tissue. Their cooperation seemed to support a healthier environment within fat tissue and better metabolic function. Male mice, however, showed a different response when exposed to a high-fat diet. They were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation, alongside weaker protective activity in their fat tissue. item.title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
item.description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained. The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa. “I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria. “Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added. On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency. Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option. Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters. He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence. “First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added. Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”. The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow. Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.” The post Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: [VIDEO] I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2.
